name: Runner Extras - Object Metadata System Table
brief: Issue #2519: Object Metadata (2000000071) is a real application-database table, not a virtual one. The runner has no application database, so it synthesises the row set from BC's own SystemTables.ApplicationDatabaseTables and leaves the compiled-metadata payload columns blank. This suite pins the synthesis and the blank payload so neither can change silently.
description: What Object Metadata CONTAINS - one row per application-database system table, Object Type = Table, nothing else - is plain BC behaviour and lives upstream. It took two attempts. Corpus PR StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#153 was withdrawn after all 8 BC legs of run 33968379281 refused the only route a Cloud-target app has: the record type does not compile (AL0296, the table is Scope = OnPrem) and RecordRef.Open is refused at runtime by NavRecordRef.CheckIsOpenAllowed, because 2000000071 is in SystemTables.InternalTables. Corpus PR #179 then added a Target = OnPrem app - the calling app's compilation target is what decides both refusals, and nothing else - and tests/al-language-onprem/record/TestObjectMetadataSystemTable.al now measures the row set on all eight OnPrem legs, BC 27.0 through 28.4: 43 rows, one per id on Microsoft's list, including the ObsoleteState = Removed and Pending ids, and no row for a virtual or ordinary application table. So the row set is service-tier-adjudicated, and this repository's corpus leg runs that same file against the runner. This suite pins what the RUNNER does, which no tier can see: that the rows appear at all with no application database behind them, that the ids track BC's own SystemTables.ApplicationDatabaseTables list, that the compiled-metadata payload columns (Metadata, User Code, User AL Code, Symbol Reference, Metadata Version, Hash, Object Subtype, Has Subscribers, Schema Hash) read blank rather than carrying a fabricated payload, and that Emit Version is a real BC build emit version rather than a chosen constant. The blank payload is a DECLARED divergence, recorded in docs/limitations.md; issue #2771 tracks making those columns refuse by name instead, which needs a per-field blob-read seam the shared TempTableDataProvider path does not have. Target is OnPrem, not Cloud: Microsoft declares Object Metadata Scope = OnPrem, so an AL object naming the record type cannot compile for Cloud (AL0296).
